symptom: PC1 (Fa0/1, VLAN 10) cannot ping its own default gateway 192.168.10.1.
topology_note: SW1 access switch, Fa0/1 assigned to PC1, uplink to R1 sub-interface Gi0/0.10 for VLAN 10.
show_command_output:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name    Status  Ports
1  default    active  Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3
10 SALES      active  Fa0/5

SW1# show interfaces fa0/1 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Fa0/1 is still in VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 10, so PC1 is on the wrong broadcast domain and cannot reach the VLAN 10 gateway.

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 20 on SW2 cannot reach hosts in VLAN 20 on SW1 across the trunk.
topology_note: SW1 <-> SW2 trunk on Gi0/1, VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 exist on both switches.
show_command_output:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port  Mode  Encapsulation  Status  Native vlan
Gi0/1 on    802.1q         trunking 1

Vlans allowed on trunk: 1,10
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is missing from the trunk's allowed VLAN list ('switchport trunk allowed vlan' does not include 20), so VLAN 20 traffic is dropped at the trunk.

symptom: PC on Fa0/8 receives a DHCP address from the wrong subnet (192.168.10.x instead of 192.168.30.x).
topology_note: Fa0/8 is meant to be in VLAN 30, DHCP relay (ip helper-address) configured on router sub-interfaces.
show_command_output:
SW1# show interfaces fa0/8 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (SALES)

R1# show run interface gi0/0.30
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 30
 ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 192.168.100.10
expected_fault: Fa0/8 was assigned to VLAN 10 instead of VLAN 30 by mistake, so the DHCP request is relayed using the VLAN 10 sub-interface's helper scope.

symptom: CDP native VLAN mismatch warning appears in the switch log between SW1 and SW2.
topology_note: Trunk between SW1 Gi0/1 and SW2 Gi0/1.
show_command_output:
SW1# show interfaces gi0/1 trunk
Native vlan: 1

SW2# show interfaces gi0/1 trunk
Native vlan: 99
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1
expected_fault: The trunk's native VLAN is set to 1 on SW1 and 99 on SW2 — a mismatched native VLAN, which risks VLAN leakage for untagged frames.

symptom: PC2 has a valid IP (192.168.10.25/24) but cannot reach any device outside its subnet.
topology_note: PC2 static IP configuration, gateway should be 192.168.10.1.
show_command_output:
PC2> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.25
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.10.10
expected_fault: Default gateway is typo'd as 192.168.10.10 instead of the router's actual interface address 192.168.10.1.

symptom: All hosts in VLAN 10 lost gateway connectivity at the same time.
topology_note: L3 switch SW1 provides the VLAN 10 SVI as the gateway.
show_command_output:
SW1# show ip interface brief
Interface       IP-Address     Status     Protocol
Vlan10          192.168.10.1   down       down
expected_fault: SVI 'interface vlan 10' is administratively down (no shutdown missing), taking down the gateway for the whole VLAN.

symptom: Gateway is intermittently unreachable; standby router sometimes answers instead of the active one.
topology_note: R1 and R2 run HSRP for VLAN 10 virtual gateway 192.168.10.1.
show_command_output:
R1# show standby brief
Interface  Grp  Pri  State   Active     Standby
Gi0/0.10   10   100  Active  local      R2

R2# show standby brief
Interface  Grp  Pri  State   Active     Standby
Gi0/0.10   10   110  Active  local      unknown
expected_fault: Both R1 and R2 report themselves as Active for HSRP group 10 (priority/preempt misconfiguration), causing an active/active split and intermittent gateway failures.

symptom: New PCs joining VLAN 10 fail to get an IP address; existing PCs are fine.
topology_note: R1 is the DHCP server for pool SALES_POOL, network 192.168.10.0/24.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL
Pool SALES_POOL:
 Address range: 192.168.10.10 - 192.168.10.14
 Leased addresses: 5
 Pending event: none

R1# show ip dhcp conflict
(none)
expected_fault: The DHCP pool's address range (only 5 usable addresses) is exhausted; the pool needs a larger range or the network/exclude statements corrected.

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 20 never receive a DHCP offer even though the DHCP server lives in VLAN 10.
topology_note: R1 is L3 gateway for both VLANs; DHCP server is a Windows server host in VLAN 10.
show_command_output:
R1# show run interface gi0/0.20
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
! (no ip helper-address configured)
expected_fault: 'ip helper-address' pointing at the DHCP server is missing on the VLAN 20 sub-interface, so DHCP broadcasts from VLAN 20 are never relayed to the server.

symptom: Clients get an IP address and mask but no internet or inter-VLAN access.
topology_note: R1 DHCP pool SALES_POOL for VLAN 10.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section dhcp pool SALES_POOL
ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
 dns-server 8.8.8.8
! (no default-router configured)
expected_fault: The DHCP pool has no 'default-router' statement, so clients never learn a gateway address even though addressing works.

symptom: PC can ping 8.8.8.8 by IP but 'ping google.com' fails to resolve.
topology_note: PC gets DNS server address via static config.
show_command_output:
PC1> ipconfig /all
DNS Server: 192.168.10.200

PC1> ping 192.168.10.200
Request timed out. (4/4 lost)
expected_fault: The configured DNS server address (192.168.10.200) does not correspond to a real DNS server on the network, so all name resolution fails while raw IP connectivity works.

symptom: Name resolution fails for all hosts in VLAN 10 only; VLAN 20 is unaffected and uses the same DNS server.
topology_note: R1 has an ACL applied inbound on Gi0/0.10 for security filtering.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
 10 deny udp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 53
 20 permit ip any any

R1# show run interface gi0/0.10
 ip access-group 110 in
expected_fault: ACL 110 explicitly denies UDP port 53 (DNS) from VLAN 10 before the permit-any statement, blocking DNS queries only from that VLAN.

symptom: Internal hostnames (e.g. fileserver.corp.local) fail to resolve, but internet domains resolve fine.
topology_note: R1 forwards DNS to both an internal DNS server and public DNS via 'ip name-server'.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | include name-server
ip name-server 8.8.8.8
! (internal DNS server 192.168.10.200 not listed)
expected_fault: Only the public DNS server is configured under 'ip name-server'; the internal DNS server that holds the corp.local zone was never added, so internal names cannot resolve.

symptom: VLAN 10 hosts can reach VLAN 20 but not the remote branch subnet 172.16.5.0/24.
topology_note: R1 (HQ) connects to R2 (branch) via a serial link; no dynamic routing configured.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip route
C  192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
C  192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20
C  10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
! no route to 172.16.5.0/24
expected_fault: R1 has no static route (or dynamic routing) for 172.16.5.0/24 via the branch link, so packets to the branch subnet are dropped at R1.

symptom: OSPF neighbors between R1 and R2 never reach the FULL state.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected via Serial0/0/0, both configured for OSPF area 0.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip ospf interface serial0/0/0
Process ID 1, Area 0

R2# show ip ospf interface serial0/0/0
Process ID 1, Area 1

R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(empty)
expected_fault: R1 advertises the shared link in area 0 while R2 advertises it in area 1 — mismatched OSPF area IDs prevent adjacency from forming.

symptom: VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24) is missing from R1's OSPF-learned routes on R2, even though R1 has OSPF configured.
topology_note: R1 runs OSPF area 0 covering its LAN interfaces.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
 network 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
! 192.168.30.0/24 network statement missing
expected_fault: The OSPF 'network' statement for 192.168.30.0/24 is missing, so that interface is never advertised into OSPF even though it is up.

symptom: Internal traffic works fine, but no host on the network can reach the internet.
topology_note: R1 connects to the ISP via Gi0/1; internal routing (OSPF) is healthy.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip route
O  192.168.10.0/24 [110/2] via ...
O  192.168.20.0/24 [110/2] via ...
! no default route (0.0.0.0/0) present

R1# show run interface gi0/1
 ip address 203.0.113.2 255.255.255.252
expected_fault: There is no default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the ISP, so internally-routed traffic has no path out to unknown external destinations.

symptom: Traffic to the branch subnet sometimes takes a slower, extra-hop path instead of the direct serial link.
topology_note: R1 redistributes static routes into OSPF; a static route and an OSPF-learned route both exist for 172.16.5.0/24.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip route 172.16.5.0
Routing entry for 172.16.5.0/24
 Known via "ospf 1", distance 110
  via 192.168.99.2 (extra hop path)
 Known via "static", distance 1
  via 10.0.0.2 (direct serial link) - not selected
expected_fault: The OSPF-learned route (AD 110) is not actually preferred here because a redistribution/metric issue is letting the higher-AD path win in this topology; the static route's administrative distance and redistribution metrics need to be reviewed so the direct link is preferred.

symptom: All traffic from VLAN 20 to the server farm is blocked, including traffic that should be explicitly permitted.
topology_note: ACL 101 applied inbound on Gi0/0.20 to restrict server access.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
 10 deny ip 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 any
 20 permit tcp 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.100.10 eq 443

R1# show run interface gi0/0.20
 ip access-group 101 in
expected_fault: A broad 'deny ip any' style statement (line 10) sits above the intended permit statement (line 20), so the permit is never reached and all VLAN 20 traffic is dropped.

symptom: An ACL meant to restrict outbound internet access has no effect at all — traffic passes regardless of the rules.
topology_note: ACL 105 written to filter traffic leaving Gi0/1 toward the ISP.
show_command_output:
R1# show run interface gi0/1
 ip access-group 105 in

R1# show access-lists 105
Extended IP access list 105
 10 deny tcp any any eq 80
 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL 105 is applied 'in' on the ISP-facing interface (filtering inbound internet traffic) instead of 'out', so it never inspects outbound traffic from internal hosts as intended.

symptom: A newly added ACL to block one host (192.168.10.50) from the server ended up blocking the entire VLAN.
topology_note: ACL 102 applied to Gi0/0.10 inbound.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 102
Extended IP access list 102
 10 deny ip host 192.168.10.50 host 192.168.100.10
! (no explicit permit statement follows)
expected_fault: Only a deny statement was written; with no explicit 'permit ip any any' after it, the ACL's implicit deny-all drops every other host's traffic too.

symptom: ACL intended to restrict VLAN 30 guest traffic appears to have zero matches, and guests still reach internal servers.
topology_note: ACL 130 was written for VLAN 30 but applied elsewhere.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | include ip access-group
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 ip access-group 130 in
! (VLAN 30 sub-interface Gi0/0.30 has no ACL applied)
expected_fault: ACL 130 was applied to the VLAN 10 sub-interface instead of the VLAN 30 (guest) sub-interface it was designed for, so guest traffic is never filtered.

symptom: Internal hosts can ping R1's outside interface but cannot reach any internet address.
topology_note: R1 configured with a NAT pool and access-list for PAT overload.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip nat translations
(empty)

R1# show run | include ip nat
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 ip nat inside
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip nat outside
! no 'ip nat inside source list ... overload' statement present
expected_fault: Interfaces are correctly marked inside/outside, but the actual NAT overload (PAT) statement binding the inside ACL to the outside interface was never configured, so no translations occur.

symptom: NAT is configured with a valid overload statement, but nothing is being translated.
topology_note: R1 has 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface gi0/1 overload' configured.
show_command_output:
R1# show run interface gi0/0.10
! (missing 'ip nat inside')

R1# show run interface gi0/1
 ip address 203.0.113.2 255.255.255.252
! (missing 'ip nat outside')
expected_fault: Neither interface has been marked with 'ip nat inside' or 'ip nat outside', so the router never applies the otherwise-correct NAT overload rule to any traffic.

symptom: Port-forwarded web server (static NAT) is unreachable from outside; internal access works fine.
topology_note: Static NAT maps public 203.0.113.10 to an internal web server.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | include ip nat inside source static
ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.10.99 80 203.0.113.10 80

! actual web server address is 192.168.10.100, not .99
expected_fault: The static NAT entry maps the public address to 192.168.10.99, but the real web server is 192.168.10.100 — a wrong internal (local) address in the mapping.

symptom: VLAN 10 gets internet access through NAT, but VLAN 20 does not, despite both using the same router.
topology_note: NAT ACL 1 defines which inside networks are translated.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 1
Standard IP access list 1
 10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
! 192.168.20.0/24 not included
expected_fault: The NAT-matching ACL only permits the VLAN 10 subnet; VLAN 20's subnet was never added, so its traffic is never selected for translation.

symptom: Laptops cannot see the corporate SSID 'CorpNet' at all in the available networks list.
topology_note: Access point configured with SSID CorpNet on VLAN 10.
show_command_output:
AP# show running-config | section dot11
dot11 ssid CorpNet
 vlan 10
 authentication open
! guest-mode not enabled / broadcast-ssid missing
expected_fault: The SSID exists but is not set to broadcast (guest-mode/broadcast-ssid not enabled), so it never appears in clients' network lists even though the radio is otherwise configured.

symptom: Wireless clients see the SSID but fail authentication every time with the correct-looking password.
topology_note: AP configured for WPA2-PSK on SSID CorpNet.
show_command_output:
AP# show run | section wpa
wpa-psk ascii 0 Summer2025!

! client profile configured with passphrase Summer2024!
expected_fault: The AP's WPA2 pre-shared key (Summer2025!) does not match the key configured in the client's wireless profile (Summer2024!), causing repeated authentication failure.

symptom: Wireless clients associate to the AP successfully but never receive an IP address.
topology_note: AP bridges SSID CorpNet to a VLAN via a trunk to SW1.
show_command_output:
AP# show run | include vlan
 vlan 30

SW1# show interfaces fa0/12 switchport
Access VLAN: 10
(AP uplink port fa0/12 is an access port, not trunk, on VLAN 10)
expected_fault: The AP is configured to bridge wireless clients into VLAN 30, but its uplink switch port is a VLAN 10 access port, so wireless client DHCP requests reach the wrong VLAN/DHCP scope (or none at all).

symptom: Wireless users near the edge of the building report frequent drops and slow speeds, worse near a specific hallway.
topology_note: Two APs (AP1, AP2) cover overlapping areas of the same floor.
show_command_output:
AP1# show controllers dot11radio 0 | include Channel
Channel: 6

AP2# show controllers dot11radio 0 | include Channel
Channel: 6
expected_fault: AP1 and AP2 are both set to channel 6 in an overlapping coverage area, causing co-channel interference and degraded performance rather than a hard outage.
